→ D3: The wait numbers come from windows that begin before any arrival press and are measured against a tap the timeline says never happened (F7), so F2's 4 min 30 s and F3's 3 min 25 s cannot by themselves satisfy NS-1(iii) read together with NS-1(i). [F2 F3 F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee charged to the rider under a driver-cancelled no-show claim fails NS-1(i): the timeline record shows the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so the first mandatory condition is not met and the fee must be refunded in full under NS-2.

The system timeline is internally inconsistent and cannot be relied on to cure the missing 'I'm Here' tap: F6 records a tap at 09:56:20, while F7 records that no tap ever occurred; because the system records govern and the required condition is absent on the authoritative record, NS-1 fails.

Even if the 'I'm Here' tap were accepted, NS-1(iii) requires the driver to wait more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01) at the pickup point; the driver's stationary period of 3 min 25 s at 38 m (F3) overlaps only 3 min 5 s within 200 m after the disputed tap (F6), and the platform-recorded waiting window is 4 min 30 s (F5) — any shortfall is not the rider's to bear, and the rider states she came out a minute after the cancellation.

The driver's chat messages and written statement asserting he pressed 'I'm Here' and waited over 3 minutes (F10, F11, F12) are user-submitted content that cannot override the timeline record showing no tap (F7), so they do not establish the NS-1 conditions.

The driver's account history shows 3 disputes and 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17), so a flag_account action for repeated cancellation/waiting-fee conduct is warranted alongside the refund, while the rider has a clean 0-dispute record (F16).

weaknesses: The rider's own statement that she came out only 'a minute after the driver cancelled' is not corroborated by any system record; the GPS shows the driver sat stationary at 38 m for 3 min 25 s (F3) and was inside 200 m cumulatively 4 min 30 s (F2, F5), which supports the driver's 'waited over 3 minutes' account (F11, F12) and may persuade the judge that service was reasonably attempted.

F6 records a driver 'I'm Here' tap at 09:56:20 and 3 min 5 s within 200 m after the tap, which, if taken at face value, would satisfy the NS-1 timing requirement and support no_action together with the $6.61 fee (F4, F8); my case for full refund therefore depends on F7 overriding F6.
The rider has 0 upheld no-show disputes and 0 disputes in 90 days (F16), but the profile is not evidence about this trip, so it cannot itself prove the rider was at the pickup point on time.

claims.assertion: Cancellation fee $6.61 (F8) is valid only via NS-0's driver-claims-rider-no-show branch, which routes to NS-1; the driver did in fact cancel and did claim a rider no-show (F4, F12).

System records confirm the driver was physically at the pickup: closest approach 38 m at 09:58:25 (F1), first inside 200 m at 09:54:55 and stationary at 38 m from 09:56:00 to cancellation at 09:59:25 (F2, F3) — satisfying NS-1(ii) 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data'.

The driver waited well over 3 minutes at the pickup point: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 4 min 30 s (F2) and the stationary period alone was 3 min 25 s (F3), exceeding the >180 s requirement of NS-1(iii).

The platform timeline independently corroborates arrival and the wait: recorded arrival 09:54:55 and cancellation 4 min 30 s after arrival (F5), and the driver messaged the rider 'I'm here at the pickup point' at 09:56 (F10) before cancelling at 09:59 (F11).

The rider's own account admits he came out only 'a minute after the driver cancelled' (i.e. after 09:59:25, over 4 minutes after the driver arrived), so the rider was not at the pickup point during the 3-minute waiting window and the rider NO SHOW condition in NS-0/NS-1 is met.

There was no congestion, incident or weather excuse for delay on the optimal route (F13 band 3 = 20–29 km/h, F14 no incidents, F15 fair weather), so nothing in the trip conditions undermines the completed wait-and-arrive record.

Even if the court declines to treat the 'I'm Here' button as pressed, the geofence and wait requirements are independently proven by GPS and timeline records (F2, F3, F5), which under the system-record priority control over the conflicting timeline entry F7 and the driver's own written statement F12.
No refund is owed: the $6.61 fee (F8) satisfies NS-1 and the correct disposition is no_action; the fee was not surge-inflated (F9), so no part of it is an unpublishable add-on.

In the alternative, if the court finds any NS-1 element unproven and orders a refund, the only correct amount is $6.61 in Ryde voucher form (F8), payable to the rider, with no additional penalty on the driver because the GPS records show he genuinely waited at the pickup (F2, F3).

The driver (F17: 1602 days on platform, 4.59 rating, 645 trips in 90 days, no-show disputes upheld) did not abuse the cancel/waiting button in a way warranting an account flag on this fee: the fee is supported by system GPS and timeline evidence, so NS-2's fraud add-on does not attach.

weaknesses: The fact table is internally contradictory on the 'I'm Here' tap: F6 says the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:56:20, 40 m from the pickup, while F7 says the driver never tapped it (driver_pressed_here_at null). The opposing side will cite F7 to argue NS-1(i) is unproven and that NS-2 (full refund of $6.61, plus account flag) applies — see D7.

The rider will rely on F5 ('Platform recorded driver arrival at 09:54:55') and his own statement that he came out one minute later to argue the driver waited barely more than the 3-minute minimum and that the driver should have given him longer; NS-1 does not, however, require any wait beyond 3:01.

The profile fact F17 shows the driver already has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, which the rider can use to argue a pattern under RD-6-style 'repeated' reasoning and to request an account flag; profile facts cannot decide this case but can support that add-on.
If the court prefers F7 over F6, the driver's own written statement F12 ('I pressed I'm Here') is contradicted by a timeline record and, per the priority rules, cannot carry the claim on its own.

points.response: Conceded only in part: the fee is chargeable solely through NS-0's driver-claims-no-show branch into NS-1, and that branch is exactly where the driver's case fails, because NS-1(i) requires an actual 'I'm Here' press and the timeline record shows driver_pressed_here_at is null (F7).
D2 is not contested — the GPS does place the driver 38 m away (F1, F2, F3) and NS-1(ii) is satisfied; but NS-1 is conjunctive, so proving (ii) alone does not make the fee valid.

The wait numbers come from windows that begin before any arrival press and are measured against a tap the timeline says never happened (F7), so F2's 4 min 30 s and F3's 3 min 25 s cannot by themselves satisfy NS-1(iii) read together with NS-1(i).

D4 proves only arrival, not compliance: the driver's own message says 'I'm here at the pickup point' (F10) but nothing in the chat shows any 'I'm Here' button press, and F12's unsworn assertion cannot fill that gap against the null timeline entry (F7).

D5 misreads the complaint: the rider's statement is that he came out a minute after the cancellation, which places him at the pickup within about a minute of 09:59:25, and NS-1(iii) sets a floor, not an entitlement for the driver to leave at exactly 3:01.
Conceded: no incident, congestion band or weather factor excuses anything here (F13 band 3 at 20–29 km/h, F14 no incidents, F15 fair), and this point is irrelevant to the NS-1(i) defect.

D7 inverts the priority rule it invokes: F7 and F6 are both system timeline records and they contradict each other, while F12 is a user statement, so the contradiction must be resolved against the side carrying the burden — the driver — and NS-2 requires the full $6.61 back when NS-1(i) is unproven (F8).

The fee is not surge-inflated (F9) and its $6.61 amount is correct (F8), but an amount fact cannot substitute for the unmet condition in NS-1(i), so no_action is the wrong disposition and refund_full under NS-2 is correct.

D9 concedes the refund amount and voucher form (F8, NS-7); I accept $6.61 as a Ryde voucher, and the account flag is requested separately on the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17), not as a penalty inside the refund amount.

D10 understates the record: the driver already has 3 disputes and 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17), and NS-2 attaches an account flag when an 'I'm Here' press is contradicted by GPS/timeline — here the timeline itself denies any press (F7).

The 'no tap' entry F7 cannot be treated as the authoritative record because it is contradicted within its own family: F6 shows a tap at 09:56:20, 40 m from the pickup, with 3 min 5 s spent inside 200 m after the tap. Where a system record is internally inconsistent, NS-1(i) is still satisfied on the record matching the independently corroborated physical facts: F2 (first inside 200 m at 09:54:55; 4 min 30 s cumulative) and F3 (stationary 3 min 25 s at 38 m), which prove the driver was at the pickup and waited regardless of which button entry is preferred.

The inconsistency the rider relies on cuts both ways but is resolved by corroboration: F6's tap at 09:56:20 is consistent with F1 (closest approach 38 m at 09:58:25) and F3 (stationary at 38 m from 09:56:00), while F7 is a bare null field with no supporting physical record. On the actual positions, the driver was demonstrably at the pickup point before and throughout the wait, so NS-1(ii) and (iii) hold independently of the tap entry.

The rider misreads NS-1(iii): the threshold is >180 s spent within 200 m of the pickup, and F2 records 4 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m, with F3 showing 3 min 25 s stationary at 38 m — both exceed 3:01 even discounting the rider's uncorroborated 'came out a minute later' account. The rider's own plea in fact concedes he appeared only after the cancellation at 09:59:25 (F4), i.e. more than 4 minutes after the 09:54:55 arrival (F5).

Conceded in part: the chat messages F10, F11 and the driver statement F12 are user-submitted and cannot by themselves cure a contested tap record. But the driver's case does not rest on them — the wait is established by the system's own GPS and timeline facts F2, F3 and F5, which are the highest-priority records and are not contradicted by any GPS fact.

Conceded in part: F17 does show 3 disputes and 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, which can be weighed under repeated-conduct reasoning, and F16 shows the rider is clean. But under NS-2 a flag_account attaches only where the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while GPS showed he was outside the pickup range — here F1 and F3 show he was 38 m away, so the fraud predicate for a flag is absent and the profile cannot itself decide the fee.

I withdraw the framing that F7 alone must be overcome by record-priority; the stronger position is that the relevant NS-1 elements are proved by GPS facts F2 and F3 and timeline F5 irrespective of the F6/F7 conflict.
